I have downloaded and installed “eM Client” and it works *perfectly*. However, I would loathe to have to abandon Thunderbird and get used to an entirely new program, but which is what I will have to do if this thing is not resolved ASAP.

As mentioned, I think there has to do with the OAuth authentication system.

I have even tried ChatGPT, without success!

And there is no way to revert to the previous version !!!!!

Please do something NOW, or it is, regrettably, goodbye Thunderbird!

title: Drag-and-drop email export to Windows Explorer no longer works in Thunderbird 153.0.2esr
creator: samsungchobg
content:
Environment:

Thunderbird: 153.0.2esr (64-bit) Operating system: Windows Occurs with multiple email accounts Reproduced on two different computers running the same Thunderbird version

Description:

After updating Thunderbird to version 153.0.2esr, released on 4 August 2026, emails can no longer be dragged and dropped from Thunderbird to the Windows Desktop or any folder in Windows Explorer.

The problem occurs with all tested email accounts and folders. It has been reproduced independently on two different Windows computers using the same Thunderbird version.

Saving an email manually with Ctrl+S works correctly and creates the .eml file. Normal drag-and-drop between folders in Windows Explorer also works. Only dragging an email from Thunderbird to Windows Explorer fails.

The issue also appears to affect third-party applications that use Thunderbird to create or send emails automatically.

Steps to reproduce:

Open Thunderbird 153.0.2esr on Windows. Select an email in any account or folder. Drag the email to the Desktop or another folder in Windows Explorer. Release the mouse button.

Actual result:

The email is not copied or saved to the selected Windows folder.

Expected result:

Thunderbird should export the email as an .eml file in the selected folder.

Additional information:

Ctrl+S successfully saves the same email. The issue affects every tested email account. Thunderbird extensions were disabled, but the problem remained. Thunderbird Troubleshoot Mode did not resolve the issue. Restarting Thunderbird, Windows Explorer and Windows did not resolve it. Thunderbird and Windows Explorer are not running with different elevation levels. The problem was reproduced on a second computer after installing the same Thunderbird version. No relevant error is shown in Thunderbird’s Error Console when the drag-and-drop operation fails. The issue was not present before the recent Thunderbird update.

This appears to be a regression in Thunderbird 153.0.2esr affecting email export through drag-and-drop and possibly Thunderbird’s integration with external applications.

title: Hotmail personal account: IMAP OAuth2 works but SMTP OAuth2 fails with message: 535 5.7.139 “SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox”
creator: joncoffey68
content:
I am assisting an elderly user with a personal @hotmail.com account that receives email successfully in Thunderbird but cannot send. I have confirmed they can send and receive emails from their online outlook.com portal. The user's computer setup is as follows:

  • Windows 11 (with latest updates).
  • Thunderbird 153.0.2 (64-bit).
  • A personal @hotmail.com account with the following server configurations: 
  -> Incoming IMAP: outlook.office365.com, port 993, SSL/TLS, OAuth2, and   -> Outgoing SMTP: smtp-mail.outlook.com, port 587, STARTTLS, OAuth2.

Thunderbird successfully authenticates to Microsoft using OAuth2 for incoming email. However, when Thunderbird attempts outgoing email authentication, Microsoft's SMTP server rejects the authentication. The Error Console in Thunderbird records this message: "535 5.7.139 Authentication unsuccessful, SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox."

-> Refer to attached image: "Thunderbird Error Console_20260811.jpg". -> I am able to provide a short screen recording demonstrating the failure if needed.

To try and resolve the above, I completed the following actions:

  1. Confirmed Thunderbird is current (153.0.2).
  2. Confirmed SMTP is configured for OAuth2 rather than Normal Password.
  3. Confirmed port 587 and STARTTLS.
  4. Re-authorised the Microsoft account/OAuth connection.
  5. Confirmed IMAP OAuth2 works.
  6. Confirmed Outlook.com webmail can send successfully.
  7. Reviewed Mozilla's current “Microsoft OAuth Authentication and Thunderbird in 2026” guidance, including the section covering cases where IMAP/POP works but SMTP does not.
  8. Captured the SMTP failure in Thunderbird's Error Console.

However nothing worked, so I raised the matter with Microsoft support and eventually had the matter referred to their Tier 2 team. The Microsoft case number is: 7107041963.

Microsoft Support confirmed that for a personal Outlook.com/Hotmail account there is no user-accessible mailbox-level SMTP AUTH setting, and advised that SMTP is enabled by default for supported clients. However, because sending from Outlook.com webmail works, Microsoft Tier 2 declined to investigate the SMTP server response further and directed me to Thunderbird support.

I am able to provide a copy of the chat transcript if needed.

In any event, the TLDR version IMAP works using OAuth2, but SMTP using OAuth2 fails because Microsoft's SMTP server reports SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox. Microsoft Tier 2 has referred the issue to Thunderbird support.

Questions:

  1. Is this a known current issue affecting personal Outlook.com/Hotmail accounts using Thunderbird?
  2. Is 535 5.7.139 SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox known to occur with Thunderbird OAuth2 even though IMAP OAuth2 succeeds?
  3. Is there a current Thunderbird-side workaround or alternative SMTP server/configuration recommended for personal Hotmail accounts?
  4. Would changing the SMTP server from smtp-mail.outlook.com to smtp.office365.com be appropriate for a personal Hotmail account in Thunderbird 153, or should the current Microsoft-documented server be retained?

-> I note there appears to be conflicting advice on this point in previous support threads.

  1. Given that IMAP OAuth2 authentication succeeds for the same Microsoft account, does this indicate that Thunderbird's Microsoft OAuth authorisation itself is functioning correctly, or could SMTP require a separate permission/token that may be failing?
  2. Are there any additional Thunderbird logs or diagnostics I can provide that would help resolve this matter?

Disclosure: I used ChatGPT to help organise my troubleshooting notes and technical details for this post. The troubleshooting, observations and diagnostic information described above are from my own work on the affected PC.

creator: td47
content:
It seems it is because BUGZILLA uses the AMAZON'S service, but there is now a RANGE of IP addresses that have been blocked, and BUGZILLA have been caught up in this mess. Please let me know which board I can use to report/ask about this issue, if it is no on here..

Here is the issue research (NOTE: I have emailed the BMO_MODS email several times, but had NO RESPONSE, so want to check if others have this issue):

Based on the error message you're receiving, Microsoft is blocking emails from your IP address because it appears on their block list. This is a Microsoft-specific issue rather than an AWS problem. When you receive a 550 5.7.1 error with the S3150 code from Microsoft domains (Hotmail, Outlook), it means Microsoft's filtering systems have identified your IP address as a source of problematic traffic. Even though you're using a managed dedicated IP and haven't intentionally violated any policies, there are several reasons this could occur: The IP address may have a poor reputation due to previous usage by another customer, spam complaints from recipients, high bounce rates, or sending patterns that Microsoft's algorithms flag as suspicious. Sometimes legitimate senders get caught in these filters. To resolve this issue, you should:
  • Contact Microsoft directly using the troubleshooting link provided in the error message (mail.live.com/mail/troubleshooting.aspx) to request delisting
  • Review your email sending practices to ensure you're following best practices (proper authentication, low complaint rates, engaged recipient lists)
  • Consider contacting AWS Support to discuss your dedicated IP's reputation and whether a new IP might be warranted
  • Ensure your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records are properly configured Microsoft maintains their own independent block lists and reputation systems, so even with AWS's managed infrastructure, you may need to work directly with Microsoft to resolve deliverability issues to their domains.

title: IMAP/SMTP server connected, but receives and send fails
creator: manishchawla619
content:
1. Thunderbird connects to my IMAP/SMTP server but neither receives nor sends mail

I am having a problem with Thunderbird on Windows with a custom-domain email account hosted by Advika Web.

      1. Account

Email address: `connect@synergyappstudio.com`

Mail hosting provider: Advika Web

The mailbox and password are confirmed to be valid because I can successfully log in to the provider's webmail using the same email address and password.

      1. Server settings provided by the hosting provider

Incoming IMAP:

  • Server: `mail.synergyappstudio.com`
  • Port: `993`
  • Connection security: SSL/TLS
  • Authentication: Normal password
  • Username: `connect@synergyappstudio.com`

Outgoing SMTP:

  • Server: `mail.synergyappstudio.com`
  • Port: `465`
  • Connection security: SSL/TLS
  • Authentication: Normal password
  • Username: `connect@synergyappstudio.com`
      1. What happens in Thunderbird

Thunderbird shows:

> Connected to mail.synergyappstudio.com

However, incoming messages are not downloaded and outgoing messages cannot be sent.

The SMTP error I received was:

> The connection to Outgoing server (SMTP) mail.synergyappstudio.com timed out.

      1. Connectivity tests

I tested the server from Windows PowerShell.

Port 993:

`Test-NetConnection mail.synergyappstudio.com -Port 993`

Result:

> RemoteAddress: 103.69.196.146 > RemotePort: 993 > TcpTestSucceeded: True

Port 465:

`Test-NetConnection mail.synergyappstudio.com -Port 465`

Result:

> RemoteAddress: 103.69.196.146 > RemotePort: 465 > TcpTestSucceeded: True

Therefore, both TCP ports are reachable from my computer.

      1. TLS tests

I also tested the actual TLS handshake rather than just TCP connectivity.

TLS 1.2 against IMAP 993 failed with:

> Unable to read data from the transport connection: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host.

TLS 1.0 against IMAP 993 produced the same result:

> Unable to read data from the transport connection: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host.

I also tested the TLS handshake against SMTP 465 and received the same "connection was forcibly closed by the remote host" result.

      1. Comparison with Outlook

There is an important comparison:

The same mailbox **successfully connects and authenticates in Classic Outlook** using the same server and credentials.

However, I am using Microsoft Office Home & Student, so Classic Outlook is not available to me as a practical permanent solution for this business email account.

Microsoft's **New Outlook** also fails to add the account and displays:

> Sign in failed. Please try again in a few minutes. You may need an app password.

The mailbox does not use Microsoft 365 authentication. It is a conventional hosting-provider IMAP/SMTP mailbox.

      1. Thunderbird troubleshooting already attempted

I have:

  • Confirmed the password works through webmail.
  • Confirmed the supplied IMAP/SMTP server names.
  • Confirmed ports 993 and 465 are reachable.
  • Confirmed SSL/TLS settings.
  • Used Normal Password authentication.
  • Used the full email address as the username.
  • Tried Thunderbird with the supplied IMAP/SMTP settings.
  • Reduced **Maximum number of server connections to cache** from the default 5 to 3 and then to 1. This did not resolve the problem.
  • Restarted Thunderbird after changing the connection-cache setting.
  • Tried Thunderbird's connection logging, but the generated log files remained 0 KB, so no useful log was produced.
      1. Additional observation

Thunderbird displays "Connected to mail.synergyappstudio.com", but the account does not actually synchronize incoming mail.

The provider's webmail works normally, and Classic Outlook works with the same mailbox.

      1. What I would like help determining

Could you please help determine whether this is:

1. A Thunderbird IMAP/SMTP compatibility issue with this particular mail server; 2. A TLS negotiation issue; 3. A Thunderbird configuration/profile issue; 4. A Windows/security-software interaction; or 5. Something specific to the mail server's IMAP/SMTP implementation?

In particular, I would like to understand why Thunderbird can establish the connection but cannot complete the IMAP/SMTP communication, while Classic Outlook works with the same server, ports and credentials.

I can provide Thunderbird version information, Troubleshooting Information, screenshots of the account configuration, or any additional diagnostic information you need.

content: Hello, T-bird gurus! Hoping someone, or a collective of someones, can help me out, as I just started using T-bird again after an intermission of over a decade, and I'm experiencing several progress-stifling and highly frustrating issues that unless easily overcome, will soon have me doubting my choice and abandoning the attempt (although I'd love not to have to). Whenever a new message is received, T-bird's pop-up notification lets me know that it has arrived, and the new message counter in the taskbar also displays an updated count, yet, more times than not, the inbox simply refuses to display the new message/s. Seems the ONLY way to get it to display in the inbox as it should is to close T-bird and re-open it... Then, there it is, sitting in the inbox, taunting me like a child that knows he's got your number when it comes to playing hide-and-seek (lil' booger!). Between this and my other T-bird issue (which I will put in a separate help request), it's got me ready to just pull the plug on TB and add my account to my company's Outlook... which I'd HATE to have to do, especially because it's setup through an enterprise account along with the rest of Microsoft's now full-subscription suite of programs that command a lifetime of automatic monthly payments in order to use them, so if I ever cut ties with that company, I might run the risk of losing access to my other email accounts. title: Thunderbird Mac freezes on startup (and a workaround).
creator: basbva
content:
I wanted to share a specific startup freeze loop I encountered today.

I had a moderate number of tabs open in Thunderbird when I quit the app. I had set up a single IMAP message filter yesterday to automatically move incoming automated text alerts into their own folder (causing about 50–60 small emails arriving in quick succession this morning at startup).

The Problem: Upon starting up, the app almost immediately choked and became unresponsive. Unlike the freeze report by another user here on August 21st.

My Workaround: After a few attempts to open Thunderbird I managed to break the freeze loop by instantly closing the single open UI window right at startup. This kept T-bird running invisibly in the macOS background. It seemed that without the need of rendering the UI, the background engine successfully completed all the IMAP syncing and filtering tasks.

When I brought Thunderbird back to the foreground, all my open tabs instantly "snapped", and the app has been perfectly stable since. I haven't tried to replicate this due to the fear of breaking the current stability.

Has anyone else recently noticed Thunderbird freezing under similar conditions lately? Let us know if this workaround helps you get past your startup freezes too!

title: Thunderbird 154 : dossiers spéciaux IMAP déplacés sous “Courrier entrant” sur plusieurs comptes
creator: jcschmitz
content:
Bonjour,

Depuis le passage à Thunderbird 154.0 (64 bits), plusieurs de mes comptes IMAP ont vu leur arborescence se modifier de façon inattendue.

Avant, j’avais une présentation de ce type :

Brouillons Envoyés Archives Indésirables Corbeille Courrier entrant Clients Fournisseurs etc.

Depuis peu, sur plusieurs comptes, les dossiers spéciaux Brouillons, Envoyés, Archives, Indésirables, Corbeille apparaissent désormais sous Courrier entrant.

Le phénomène touche notamment :

un compte Orange ; un compte hébergé sur un domaine personnel ; un autre compte professionnel IMAP.

En revanche, un compte Free reste affiché correctement.

En comparant les abonnements IMAP, je constate que :

sur le compte Free, Sent, Trash, etc. sont réellement à la racine du serveur, tandis que les dossiers personnels sont sous INBOX ; sur les comptes qui posent problème, les dossiers spéciaux et les dossiers personnels sont tous sous INBOX.

J’ai essayé le paramètre :

Paramètres serveur > Avancés > Dossier sur le serveur IMAP = INBOX

Cela fait bien remonter les dossiers spéciaux au niveau du compte, mais cela remonte également tous les dossiers personnels, donc l’arborescence devient entièrement plate.

J’ai également constaté qu’un déplacement manuel peut produire une erreur du serveur du type :

Client tried to access nonexistent namespace. Mailbox name should probably be prefixed with: INBOX.

Je cherche donc à savoir :

Thunderbird 154 a-t-il modifié la façon dont les dossiers spéciaux IMAP (Sent, Drafts, Trash, etc.) sont affichés lorsqu’ils sont physiquement sous INBOX ? Existe-t-il un réglage permettant de conserver les dossiers personnels sous Courrier entrant, tout en affichant les dossiers spéciaux au niveau du compte comme auparavant ? S’agit-il d’un comportement connu ou d’un bug de la version 154 ?

Je peux fournir les paramètres IMAP avancés et les captures des fenêtres S’abonner si nécessaire.

Merci.

title: Suddenly can't send/receive emails
creator: chafer444
content:
This past Saturday (21st) I noticed it was taking longer to get emails from Spectrum. I had to click the Get Messages button several times and eventually the box to put in my password would pop up. After putting it in the emails would finally show up. This continued into Sunday, but by late afternoon I was getting no emails from Spectrum. I tried sending a test email from Thunderbird and got the following error message:

An error occurred while sending mail: Outgoing server (SMTP) error. The server responded: impout007.msg.chrl.nc.charter.net cmsmtp [my IP address] blocked. Please see https://www.spectrum.net/support/internet/understanding-email-error-codes for more information. AUP#Out-1120.

I went to the Spectrum website to look up the error message and found this:

The IP address you’re trying to connect from has an issue with the Domain Name System (DNS). Spectrum requires a full circle DNS for emails to be allowed through. Verify the IP you’re connecting from, and check the IP address to ensure a reverse DNS entry exists for the IP.

At that point I called Spectrum tech support, spent about 2 hours talking to 3 different people, but I got no solution. I was able to verify my IP address is not blocked. I was basically told everything is fine on their end, so I should contact Thunderbird. All of my emails are still on the Spectrum website. I can send and receive on that site. No changes have been made to account settings or my password. I’ve tried to find an answer using Google and Youtube, but nothing so far. I did look on the Thunderbird forum, found a post from someone who was also having trouble with their emails and Spectrum this weekend. I’ve downloaded the latest version of Thunderbird, 153.1. One of the tech people suggested I use the Repair tool in Thunderbird on one of my folders. I wish I hadn’t. I used it on the Inbox folder and all of my emails disappeared in Thunderbird. They’re still on Spectrum’s site. If anyone has an idea for a solution I’d appreciate it.

As I was about to post this I opened Thunderbird and about half of the emails from my In Box have reappeared.

title: Every time Thunderbird queries gmail, it starts downloading my hundreds of thousands of emails
creator: rokaskasiliauskas
content: This post is more for posterity than asking for a solution because all similar topics ended up being Avast antivirus interfering or something less nefarious. In my case eM client started having this problem first, then I switched to TB, but the same issue here. Of all places, the best clue was found on [[Linux mint|https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?t=213352]] forums. It was a permission problem. Right click on C:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird -> properties -> security. I did two things and not sure which one did it, but they pretty much achieve the same. The Users group in the list only had read permissions so I gave it full access to the folder and checked the option to set the same permission changes to all subfolders. I also added my own personal user to that list and gave that full permissions. Oh yeah, also changed owner to myself from whatever default windows group was there before. Now, do I know the full repercussions of doing this? No. Pretty sure this just created a security hole inside my C drive, but... I don't really care at this point. If I had to fix this again, a solution might be to instruct TB to store the the email files somewhere else rather than where it is installed itself (somewhere less locked down than Program Files).

title: Puste strony i brak podglądu przy drukowaniu załączników PDF (Canon MF450, Windows 11)

content: Dzień dobry, Zgłaszam powtarzający się błąd w programie Thunderbird. Mam problem z drukowaniem załączników w formacie PDF bezpośrednio z okna wiadomości e-mail. Opis problemu: Podczas próby wydruku załącznika PDF, w oknie podglądu pojawia się czarny ekran z komunikatem, że aplikacja nie obsługuje podglądu. Po kliknięciu „Drukuj”, drukarka wypuszcza całkowicie puste, białe kartki. Środowisko: System operacyjny: Windows 11 Drukarka: Canon MF450 Series UFR II Ważne informacje: Drukarka jest w 100% sprawna. Drukowanie tych samych plików PDF po zapisaniu ich na dysku (przez przeglądarkę, Adobe Acrobat) działa bez najmniejszego problemu. Problem występuje wyłącznie wewnątrz Thunderbirda. Co już próbowałam zrobić (bez skutku): Uruchomienie programu w trybie rozwiązywania problemów (Safe Mode). Czyszczenie pamięci podręcznej (cache). Resetowanie ustawień profilu drukarki w Edytorze ustawień (usunięcie parametrów print_printer). Wymuszenie systemowego okna dialogowego przez zmianę print.prefer_system_dialog na true. Wyłączenie zaawansowanych funkcji drukowania w sterowniku Windows i zmiana trybu na rastrowy. Wygląda na to, że wbudowany silnik czytnika PDF w Thunderbirdzie przestał poprawnie komunikować się ze sterownikiem Canon UFR II. Będę wdzięczna za zbadanie tego błędu i pomoc, ponieważ drukowanie bezpośrednio z programu jest mi niezbędne do codziennej pracy. Z poważaniem, Alina

title: Why so many problems with 154.0 (aarch64)?
creator: joel.kovarsky
content:
I don't know where to start. Ever since the update to version 154 I've been having one problem after another: switch from Comcast to Yahoo causes problems with THunderbird, slow indexing, arbitrary folders showing up in different email addresses (confuses my account with my wife's' some of that may be problems dealing with gmail issues), lost email folders after attempted repairs. Three months ago there were none of these problems. I have not yet tried switching back to the last updated version of 153, but 154 does seem to have many more problems. I've run troubleshooting.

I am not a computer expert and there is only so much time I can devote to this, but even computer repair services I've called are at a loss and very pessimistic about the ability to repair things. In all the years (over a decade) my wife and I have used Thunderbird, there have never been as many problems as have surfaced in the last two months. Maybe the best that can be done is to hope that updated versions will gradually fix these issues. I will say that my Macbook Air (M2 chip) has far more problems than my iMac (M1 chip). I have checked and rechecked all server settings (smtp and imap). Although more cumbersome, things perhaps work better if I just stick to webmail options.

title: При пересылке письма удаляются вложения
creator: admin1068
content:
Добрый день.

При пересылке полученного письма с вложениями от абонента (у абонента почтовый клиент от компании 1С) вложения исчезают. Выяснили, что когда письмо отправляется из 1С "Content-Type: multipart/mixed" , Thunderbird не распознает данный параметр и поэтому удаляет вложения.

Подскажите, какие настройки сделать в почтовом клиенте, чтобы вложения не пропадали?


С уважением, Дмитрий

title: Message storage for Local Folders and accounts
creator: kaufmann
content:
TB guidance is to maintain separate profiles for dual-booting (Kubuntu and Win11), rather than sharing the profile. That adds to IMAP churn, but also to disk space, of course. But the biggest concern is keeping Local Folders (a very large archive which is by far the largest part of my profile) coordinated: both sides must access the same Local Folders.

The option to specify "Message Storage" for Local Folders obviously addresses that problem: both Kubuntu and Win11 can have the same NTFS Local Folders storage. At the same time, each IMAP account also has the option to specify its own "Message Storage" "Local Directory" location outside of the profile folder. That suggests two obvious questions:

  1. Why not specify shared storage for each account, as well as for Local Folders?
  2. After Local Folders and all accounts are shared, then precisely what, from each profile, cannot be shared between Kubuntu and Windows? Does this bring us back to asking why the profile cannot simply be shared?

[Years ago, when my email accounts were POP, I had no problem sharing a profile between WinXP and an earlier Ubuntu variant. (Of course with POP, they had to share.) Is today's separate-profiles guidance related to IMAP accounts or to some other change in TB design?]
